AgentType.description:
How HackAgent talks to a model or agent.

Chat-completion types (``LITELLM``, ``OPENAI``, ``OLLAMA``,
``LANGCHAIN``) are driven through LiteLLM. ``GOOGLE_ADK``,
``CLAUDE_CODE``, ``CODEX``, ``HERMES`` and ``WEB`` use dedicated adapters.
``MCP`` and ``A2A`` are placeholders. ``UNKNOWN`` is the fallback when a
type cannot be inferred.
AgentType.title: AgentType

AttackSpec.description:
One attack technique to run against the target: which one, how to tune it,
and which helper models it drives.

name.description: The technique to run, e.g. ``flipattack`` or ``tap``. It must be one of the registered attacks.
name.title: Name

parameters.description: The technique's own settings. Valid keys differ per attack; anything you leave out keeps its default. Each attack's page lists its parameters.
parameters.title: Parameters

roles.description: The helper models an adaptive attack uses, keyed by role name (for example ``attacker``). Static attacks need none. Each attack's page lists the roles it requires.
roles.title: Roles

AttackSpec.title: AttackSpec

AuditSpec.description:
Measure the judge panel against labelled samples before trusting it.

Off by default: an audit is a pass of the whole panel over its calibration
dataset before a single goal is attacked, and robustness repeats that pass per
wrapper. Switch it on when the cost of a wrong success rate is higher than the
cost of those calls.

enabled.description: Run the audit before the first attack.
enabled.title: Enabled

on_failure.description: What happens when the panel fails its robustness check. ``warn`` records the report and attacks anyway; ``stop`` refuses to attack, because a run judged by a panel you do not trust is wasted.
on_failure.title: On Failure

dataset.description: Which labelled samples to measure the panel against, and how many.

robustness.description: Re-judge every sample under content-preserving rewrites. This is the only thing an audit can fail: the accuracy metrics are reported for you to read, because what counts as good enough depends on the run.

AuditSpec.title: AuditSpec

CalibrationSpec.description: Which labelled dataset to measure a judge on, and how much of it.

dataset.description: Labelled dataset to measure judges against. Currently HarmBench's human-labelled classifier validation set.
dataset.title: Dataset

revision.description: Git revision of the source repository, pinned for reproducibility.
revision.title: Revision

sample_size.description: How many samples to draw. ``None`` uses the whole dataset.
sample_size.title: Sample Size

seed.description: Random seed for drawing the sample, so audits are repeatable.
seed.title: Seed

cache_dir.description: Where downloads are kept. Defaults to ``~/.cache/hackagent``.
cache_dir.title: Cache Dir

download_timeout.description: Seconds to wait when downloading the dataset.
download_timeout.title: Download Timeout

CalibrationSpec.title: CalibrationSpec

CampaignDatasetSpec.description:
Where the goals come from and which of them to run.

Goals are loaded from the ``source``, optionally labelled by the
``classifier``, then narrowed down by the ``selection``.

preset.description: Name of a built-in benchmark, e.g. ``harmbench`` or ``advbench``. Used when ``source.type`` is ``preset`` (the default).
preset.title: Preset

source.description: Where to load goals from when not using a preset.

selection.description: Which of the loaded goals to run.

classifier.description: A model that labels each goal with the risk taxonomy. Only needed when ``selection.filters.categories`` is set. Off by default.

CampaignDatasetSpec.title: CampaignDatasetSpec

CampaignMetadata.description: A name for the run, used in logs, stored results and output file names.

name.description: Short human-readable name for this campaign, e.g. ``Quick jailbreak check``.
name.title: Name

description.description: Optional free-text notes about what this campaign tests and why.
description.title: Description

CampaignMetadata.title: CampaignMetadata

CategoryClassifierConfig.description: A model that labels each goal with the risk taxonomy before the run.

name.description: The model to use, as the provider names it, e.g. ``gpt-4o-mini`` or ``llama3``. Also used to label the model in results.
name.title: Name

options.description: Settings specific to one kind of agent that are neither connection nor sampling, e.g. the ``binary`` path of a CLI agent, ADK's ``user_id``, or a web target's CSS selectors.
options.title: Options

batch_size.description: How many goals to label per request. Lower it if a small model loses track of the numbering.
batch_size.title: Batch Size

CategoryClassifierConfig.title: CategoryClassifierConfig

ConcurrencySpec.description: How much work may be in flight at once, shared by every attack.

attack.description: How many goals may be generating requests at the same time.
attack.title: Attack

target.description: How many requests may be waiting on the target at the same time.
target.title: Target

judge.description: How many replies may be judged at the same time.
judge.title: Judge

ConcurrencySpec.title: ConcurrencySpec

ConnectionSpec.description:
How to reach a model: which client to use, where it lives, and how to
authenticate.

provider.description: A label for who serves the model (``openai``, ``ollama``, ``vllm``, ``local``…). Informational only: launch tooling reads it, but the request path uses ``type``.
provider.title: Provider

type.description: Which client talks to the model. This is the field that matters: it decides whether HackAgent calls a chat API (``OPENAI``, ``OLLAMA``, ``LITELLM``…) or drives an agent directly (``CLAUDE_CODE``, ``GOOGLE_ADK``, ``WEB``…).

endpoint.description: Base URL of the model's API, e.g. ``http://localhost:11434`` for Ollama. Leave unset for local agents such as ``CLAUDE_CODE``, which run on this machine.
endpoint.title: Endpoint

api_key_env.description: Name of the environment variable that holds the API key, e.g. ``OPENAI_API_KEY``. The key itself never goes in the campaign file.
api_key_env.title: Api Key Env

headers.description: Extra HTTP headers sent with every request.
headers.title: Headers

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for one reply before giving up.
timeout.title: Timeout

ConnectionSpec.title: ConnectionSpec

DatasetFilters.description: Keep only goals that match these filters.

categories.description: Risk taxonomy categories or subcategories to keep, as a code (``E``, ``E2``) or a name (``Cybersecurity Threats``). Matched on each goal's labels, so it needs ``dataset.classifier``.
categories.title: Categories

DatasetFilters.title: DatasetFilters

DatasetSelection.description: Which of the loaded goals to run, and in what order.

limit.description: Run at most this many goals. Leave unset to run them all.
limit.title: Limit

shuffle.description: Shuffle the goals before applying ``limit``, so a limited run is a random sample instead of the first goals in the file.
shuffle.title: Shuffle

seed.description: Random seed for ``shuffle``, so the same sample is drawn every run.
seed.title: Seed

DatasetSelection.title: DatasetSelection

DatasetSource.description:
Where goals are loaded from: a built-in preset, a provider such as
HuggingFace or a local file, or goals written inline.

type.description: ``preset`` loads a built-in benchmark named by ``dataset.preset``; ``provider`` loads from ``provider`` with the fields below; ``inline`` uses the ``goals`` listed here.
type.title: Type

provider.description: For ``type: provider``: where to load from — ``huggingface``, ``file`` (a local JSON/JSONL/CSV file) or ``url_json`` (a JSON file at a URL).
provider.title: Provider

path.description: For ``type: provider``: the HuggingFace dataset id (e.g. ``walledai/AdvBench``), or the path of the local file.
path.title: Path

name.description: For HuggingFace datasets with several configurations: which one to load.
name.title: Name

split.description: For HuggingFace datasets: which split to read (``train``, ``test``…).
split.title: Split

goal_field.description: Name of the column or key that holds the goal text, e.g. ``prompt``.
goal_field.title: Goal Field

goals.description: For ``type: inline``: the goals themselves, one string per goal.
goals.title: Goals

options.description: Any other provider setting, passed through unchanged (e.g. ``url`` for ``url_json``, ``trust_remote_code`` for HuggingFace).
options.title: Options

DatasetSource.title: DatasetSource

EvaluationSpec.description:
The judge panel that scores every reply from the target.

Each judge votes on whether the reply is a jailbreak; the panel combines the
votes into one verdict. A judge that fails or answers unreadably abstains
instead of voting.

judges.description: The judge models. With no judges, replies are recorded but never scored.
judges.title: Judges

aggregation.description: How votes combine into one verdict. ``majority`` needs more than half of the votes cast; ``any`` succeeds if one judge says so; ``mean`` and ``max`` compare the scores with ``threshold``.
aggregation.title: Aggregation

threshold.description: Score a reply must reach to count as a success, on a 0 to 10 scale.
threshold.title: Threshold

require_all_judges.description: Count a reply as unsuccessful when any judge abstains.
require_all_judges.title: Require All Judges

audit.description: Measure this panel against labelled samples before the run relies on it.

EvaluationSpec.title: EvaluationSpec

ExecutionSpec.description:
How the run behaves: ordering, limits, error handling, output and storage.
Every field has a safe default.

mode.description: Run attacks one after another, or all at once within the shared limits.
mode.title: Mode

dry_run.description: Validate and build everything, but send no request.
dry_run.title: Dry Run

preflight.description: Ping the target and each judge before attacking, so an unreachable endpoint fails fast with a clear message instead of mid-run.
preflight.title: Preflight

on_error.description: After an attack fails, run the remaining ones or stop.
on_error.title: On Error

escalate.description: Run attacks in order and drop a goal once an attack jailbreaks it, so later attacks only face the goals still standing. Implies sequential order; the remaining attacks are skipped once every goal has fallen.
escalate.title: Escalate

per_attack_timeout.description: Maximum seconds a single attack may run before it is stopped and marked failed. Leave unset for no limit.
per_attack_timeout.title: Per Attack Timeout

concurrency.description: How much work may run in parallel.

retries.description: Extra attempts after a provider error.

ExecutionSpec.title: ExecutionSpec

GenerationSpec.description:
Sampling settings applied to every request the model receives. All optional:
anything left unset uses the provider's own default.

temperature.description: Randomness of the reply. ``0`` is the most deterministic.
temperature.title: Temperature

top_p.description: Nucleus sampling: only consider the most likely tokens whose probabilities add up to this value.
top_p.title: Top P

seed.description: Fixed random seed, for repeatable replies where the provider supports it.
seed.title: Seed

stop.description: Text (or list of texts) at which the model stops writing.
stop.title: Stop

reasoning_effort.description: How hard a reasoning model should think (``low``, ``medium``, ``high``), for providers that support it.
reasoning_effort.title: Reasoning Effort

response_format.description: Ask for a structured reply, e.g. ``{"type": "json_object"}``.
response_format.title: Response Format

extra_body.description: Any other provider-specific request fields, passed through unchanged.
extra_body.title: Extra Body

thinking.description: Turn a model's thinking mode on or off. Judges default to off.
thinking.title: Thinking

GenerationSpec.title: GenerationSpec

GuardrailModelConfig.description: A guardrail: a classifier model that decides whether a text is safe.

name.description: The model to use, as the provider names it, e.g. ``gpt-4o-mini`` or ``llama3``. Also used to label the model in results.
name.title: Name

options.description: Settings specific to one kind of agent that are neither connection nor sampling, e.g. the ``binary`` path of a CLI agent, ADK's ``user_id``, or a web target's CSS selectors.
options.title: Options

system_prompt.description: Replace the classifier's built-in instruction with your own.
system_prompt.title: System Prompt

GuardrailModelConfig.title: GuardrailModelConfig

GuardrailsSpec.description:
Classifier models that defend the target.

``before`` checks each prompt and blocks an unsafe one before it reaches the
target; ``after`` checks the reply and withholds an unsafe one. Both fail open:
an unavailable or unparseable classifier lets the text through, so a
misconfigured guardrail never blocks the whole run. Use this to measure an
attack against a *defended* target.

before.description: Classifier that checks each prompt before it reaches the target.

after.description: Classifier that checks each reply before it is returned.

GuardrailsSpec.title: GuardrailsSpec

JudgeSpec.description:
A judge: a model that reads the target's reply and decides whether the
attack succeeded, plus how its answer is scored.

name.description: The model to use, as the provider names it, e.g. ``gpt-4o-mini`` or ``llama3``. Also used to label the model in results.
name.title: Name

options.description: Settings specific to one kind of agent that are neither connection nor sampling, e.g. the ``binary`` path of a CLI agent, ADK's ``user_id``, or a web target's CSS selectors.
options.title: Options

scoring.description: Which judge prompt and parser this model uses.

JudgeSpec.title: JudgeSpec

ModelConfig.description:
A model HackAgent talks to: its name, how to reach it, and how to sample from
it.

The same shape describes the target, every attack helper (role), every judge,
every guardrail and the goal classifier.

name.description: The model to use, as the provider names it, e.g. ``gpt-4o-mini`` or ``llama3``. Also used to label the model in results.
name.title: Name

options.description: Settings specific to one kind of agent that are neither connection nor sampling, e.g. the ``binary`` path of a CLI agent, ADK's ``user_id``, or a web target's CSS selectors.
options.title: Options

ModelConfig.title: ModelConfig

OutputSpec.description: Files written for each run, next to the results stored in the database.

directory.description: Folder where run files are written.
directory.title: Directory

run_id.description: Fixed id for the run. Leave unset to generate a new one each time.
run_id.title: Run Id

formats.description: File formats to write: ``json`` (one document) and/or ``jsonl`` (one line per attempt).
formats.title: Formats

save_prompts.description: Include the prompts sent to the target.
save_prompts.title: Save Prompts

save_traces.description: Include the search traces of adaptive attacks (every call they made).
save_traces.title: Save Traces

OutputSpec.title: OutputSpec

RetrySpec.description: Extra attempts after a provider error (timeouts, rate limits, 5xx).

target.description: Extra attempts for a failed call to the target.
target.title: Target

roles.description: Extra attempts for a failed call to an attack's helper models.
roles.title: Roles

judges.description: Extra attempts for a failed call to a judge.
judges.title: Judges

RetrySpec.title: RetrySpec

RobustnessSpec.description:
Which rewrites to re-judge every sample under, and how many may land.

Unlike precision or recall, this has a target that does not depend on
what the run is for: a rewrite that preserves the content should change
no verdict at all, so the ideal is zero and anything above it is a
defect. That is what makes it worth gating on.

enabled.description: Re-judge every calibration sample under each wrapper.
enabled.title: Enabled

wrappers.description: Content-preserving rewrites to apply, e.g. ``prepend_append``, ``refusal_prefix``, ``educational_framing``. A good judge gives the same verdict with or without them.
wrappers.title: Wrappers

max_flip_rate.description: Largest share of a judge's verdicts a wrapper may change.
max_flip_rate.title: Max Flip Rate

RobustnessSpec.title: RobustnessSpec

ScoringSpec.description:
How a judge's reply is read: which prompt the judge gets and how its answer
is parsed into a score.

type.description: Which judge prompt and parser to use. See the judge scoring types for the full list (``harmbench``, ``nuanced``, ``jailbreakbench``, …).
type.title: Type

system_prompt.description: Replace the judge's built-in instruction with your own. Leave unset to use the instruction that matches ``type``.
system_prompt.title: System Prompt

ScoringSpec.title: ScoringSpec

StorageSpec.description: Where results are recorded so they can be browsed later.

backend.description: ``local`` writes to a SQLite file on this machine; ``remote`` sends results to a HackAgent server.
backend.title: Backend

base_url.description: Address of the remote server. Required when ``backend`` is ``remote``.
base_url.title: Base Url

api_key_env.description: Name of the environment variable holding the remote server's API key. Required when ``backend`` is ``remote``.
api_key_env.title: Api Key Env

StorageSpec.title: StorageSpec

description:
A complete campaign: what to attack, with what, and how to judge it.

It reads top to bottom as the run does: load the ``dataset``, send every goal
through each of the ``attacks`` to the ``target`` (optionally behind
``guardrails``), score the replies with the ``evaluation`` judges, and run it
all under the ``execution`` policy.

version.description: Version of the campaign format. Always ``1``.
version.title: Version

campaign.description: Name and description of the run.

dataset.description: Where the goals come from and which of them to run.

target.description: The model or agent under test.

guardrails.description: Classifier models wrapped around the target. Off by default.

attacks.description: The attack techniques to run. At least one.
attacks.title: Attacks

evaluation.description: The judge panel that decides whether each reply is a jailbreak.

execution.description: How the run behaves. Every field has a safe default.

title: HackAgent campaign
